clue.text: Carrier crossing those who: were late

definitions.text: Carrier crossing those who: were late

parts.words: Carrier crossing those who: were late
parts.note: the late are the dead, and the carrier is the mythical boatman who ferried them over the Styx

explanation.surface: A delivery service whose customers turned up after closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The late' means the dead here, not the unpunctual; the ferryman of Greek myth carried dead souls across the river Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this figure is the ferryman who rows the souls of the dead across to Hades.

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to go is to function or work, as a machine does

explanation.surface: A van comes with its day's workload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workload' splits: 'work' gives GO and 'load' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods carried by a ship or vehicle, its freight.

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
mire is mud or bog

explanation.surface: A supporter notices mud on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is a devotee or follower.

clue.text: Liable to be shot at there and then

definitions.meaning: placed in a position of exposure or difficulty

explanation.surface: An exposed target is hit at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both in a difficult, exposed position and immediately where something happens.

parts.note: bars are things that stop or block passage
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Someone stops a man named Bill from taking a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

parts.note: ado means fuss
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors make a fuss about the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate or embellish it.

definitions.meaning: to pinch is to steal or grab
a bit is a mouthpiece for a horse; this is a simple jointed kind

explanation.surface: Someone takes a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a slang verb for stealing and a type of horse's mouthpiece.

parts.note: the direction in which a clock's hands move, read as 'the way of the hands'

explanation.surface: The convenient route.
explanation.definitionFit: This direction is the way the hands of a clock turn round its face.

parts.note: a professional sportsman is a pro
a mote is a speck of dust

explanation.surface: A professional sportsman is hired to do extra dusting.
explanation.definitionFit: To further a cause is to advance or support it.

clue.text: Figure there isn't a horse willing

parts.note: no, as in 'no entry', says there isn't any
a nag is an old horse
'I'm on' means I'm willing or game

explanation.surface: Someone notes that no horse is willing to run.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

definitions.meaning: days set aside by the church for fasting
ember suggests ash, and Ash Wednesday is itself a fast day

explanation.surface: Periods of fasting such as the start of Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' means abstaining from food, not speedy; embers and ashes are what a fire leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarterly church days of fasting and prayer; their name links to the glowing remains of a fire, like ash.

definitions.meaning: a qualified craftsman employed by a master rather than working for himself
one who makes a journey, as the word's first half suggests

explanation.surface: A hired hand who is always on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired skilled worker employed by someone else; the word also reads as one who goes on a voyage.

indicators.note: only the front half of the town's name is kept

parts.note: Fakenham is a market town in Norfolk

explanation.surface: One half of a Norfolk town is a sham.
explanation.walkthrough: FAKENHAM is a market town in Norfolk, the English county; 'half of' keeps its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something phoney is counterfeit or not genuine.

clue.text: Fasten pieces the wrong way round

indicators.note: says the word for pieces is to be read backwards

parts.note: parts are pieces

explanation.surface: Someone has fastened the components back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' turns PARTS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap something is to fasten or secure it with a band.

parts.note: in cricket a single is one run
out means dismissed, a failure for the batsman

explanation.surface: A cricketer picks between getting out and taking a single.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a single is one run scored and being out means dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: To single out is to pick one particular person or thing.

clue.text: Ice store broken into in secret

indicators.note: a store that is broken into is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Burglars broke into an ice store in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken into' rearranges the eight letters of ICE STORE; 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a select few, kept private or obscure.

clue.text: Local site adapted to take swing

indicators.note: something adapted is changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A local site has been converted to house a playground swing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges the letters of LOCAL SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to move back and forth like a pendulum.

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral for one
mated means paired or married

explanation.surface: A lively newspaper piece about a single person getting married.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated describes someone spirited and full of life.

parts.note: a mate is a friend
the lot means everything

explanation.surface: A sailor hands his friend all he owns.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang, from French, for a seaman.

clue.text: Valley company given New Year honour

parts.note: the MBE is a British honour often given in the New Year Honours list

explanation.surface: A firm's boss receives a New Year honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour awarded in lists at New Year.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short narrow valley, especially in southern England.

clue.text: Scotsman in Eden for making roads

parts.note: Mac is a traditional name for a Scot
Adam was the man in the Garden of Eden

explanation.surface: A Scot in paradise is building roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Layers of compacted broken stone used as road surfacing, named after a Scottish engineer.

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lot is fate or chance, as in casting lots

explanation.surface: An idiot happens to get hold of a can-opener by luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid person.

definitions.meaning: the Royal Scot was a famous express train and locomotive class between London and Glasgow
a historic infantry regiment of the British Army

explanation.surface: A Scottish regiment drills its recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like a verb but is the plural of a famous British express locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a British army regiment and the plural of a named London-Glasgow express train.

clue.text: Went by bus round horse show

parts.note: to ride on a bus is to travel by it, so rode means went by bus
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone took the bus to an equestrian event.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibition of cowboy skills, riding broncos and roping cattle.

clue.text: Roadman takes public trans port to Peterhead

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport; the print splits the word

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A road worker catches public transport to the Scottish port of Peterhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterhead is a Scottish fishing port, but here it splits: 'head' takes the first letter of 'Peter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a vagrant who lives on the road.

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
a lid covers a container
E is the compass point east

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at cover-point has a clash with an army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover-point' looks like the cricket fielding position but splits into cover (LID) and point (E, a compass direction).
explanation.definitionFit: To collide is to crash or clash together.

parts.note: bands are groups of musicians
saw means noticed

explanation.surface: Musicians spotted someone cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A power saw with a continuous blade loop, a cutting tool.

clue.text: Forces display to take a beating

definitions.meaning: a military show of drill and music by the armed forces

explanation.surface: Soldiers parade for a show that will be roundly criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: A military parade at night, and also a rapping drumbeat such as a bugle-and-drum call.

clue.text: Unite to get side into a higher division

parts.note: a team is a side in sport
a promoted club goes up

explanation.surface: A club joins forces to win promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To join together with others to cooperate.
